scope:
Export the declared 64-zone mixture sweep and median-carbon128 comparison.

Default plotting uses the compact CSV and provenance JSON only. --rebuild-data
re-reads the exact run directories, checks constraints, and rewrites compact data.

comparison.all_series: Prescribed spherical hot inflow, fixed pulse mass and enclosed-mass density/temperature profiles within each stage; fixed physical duration; compression-cap viscosity; full 27-isotope/194-rate network; grey opacity 0.001 m2/kg.
comparison.frozen64_equal_energy: Frozen nuclear rates, 64 zones; total prepared energy fixed by adjusting radial velocity.
comparison.frozen64_fixed_flow: Frozen nuclear rates, 64 zones; radial velocity fixed, so total prepared energy varies with composition. Shared baseline rows reuse the identical equal-energy input at H/catalyst 1,1,2,1.
comparison.median_carbon128_equal_energy: 128 zones and the public median 12C(p,gamma)13N / 13C(p,gamma)14N rate updates together; total prepared energy fixed. These points change both numerical resolution and the two rate pairs relative to the faint curve.
comparison.gain: Recorded nuclear release minus modeled weak-energy escape, divided by initial internal-plus-bulk-kinetic prepared energy; (nuclear_energy_J - weak_energy_escaped_upper_J) / initial_energy_J. Subsequent radiative escape is not subtracted from this deposited-at-production gain. It is a hot-pulse diagnostic, not a whole-plant electrical gain.
comparison.line_scope: Straight segments join sampled 64-zone cases as a visual guide. No smoothed optimum or unrun case is inferred.
comparison.uncertainty: No error bars: these datasets are different modeling choices, not draws defining a confidence or credible interval. Mesh convergence and source formation remain separate studies.

rate_update.outside_table: Constant endpoint new/old ratio; relevant trajectories remain within table during burn.
rate_update.reverse_policy: Identical multiplicative factor for each forward/reverse pair, preserving the original library equilibrium ratio and Q.
